ISSUE TITLE: BOM stations() returns a silently partial catalog when KiWIS 500s
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters

`BOMCollector.stations()` (added in #276) issues one `getStationList` request per BOM parameter type, because an unfiltered response leaves `parametertype_name` blank on ~76% of rows. Each request is wrapped in its own `try/except` (`collectors/bom.py:186-193`): a failure is logged as a warning and the loop continues.

BOM's KiWIS gateway returns intermittent 500s. #208 noted this when the issue was written, and it is still true: two consecutive live runs of `stations(variable="water_quality")` on 2026-08-27 returned **1,113** and **3,759** stations, against roughly 4,400 when every request succeeds. Nothing in the return value says which is which.

That is a problem specifically because of what consumes it. `registry.harvest_stations` gives every source a `StationCatalog` with an `error` field (`registry.py:522-529`) so a dead source is visible to the weekly Archive harvest:

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad source must not sink the others
    logger.warning("[%s] station lookup failed: %s", key, exc)
    return StationCatalog(source=key, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", ...)
```

BOM never raises, so `error` stays empty and the harvest records a truncated Australian catalog as a clean success. BOM is currently the only source that can do this, because it is the only one making N requests per call.

## What to build

Track the parameter types that failed and let the caller see them. Roughly:

- Collect failed types in a list instead of only logging each one.
- If **every** request failed, raise rather than return `[]`, so `StationCatalog.error` fires and the harvest reports the source as down.
- If **some** failed, surface it: either a summary warning naming the types (cheapest) or a structured field the harvest can record, so a partial catalog is distinguishable from a complete one.

The existing per-request `try/except` should stay. A partial Australian catalog is better than none; it just should not be silently indistinguishable from a full one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run where every parameter-type request fails raises instead of returning an empty list
- [ ] A run where some requests fail reports which types were lost, not just a count of dropped rows
- [ ] A fully successful run behaves exactly as it does today
- [ ] Tests cover all three cases with a mocked client (see `tests/test_collectors/test_stations.py`, which already mocks per-parameter-type payloads)

ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters

`BOMCollector.stations()` (added in #276) issues one `getStationList` request per BOM parameter type, because an unfiltered response leaves `parametertype_name` blank on ~76% of rows. Each request is wrapped in its own `try/except` (`collectors/bom.py:186-193`): a failure is logged as a warning and the loop continues.

BOM's KiWIS gateway returns intermittent 500s. #208 noted this when the issue was written, and it is still true: two consecutive live runs of `stations(variable="water_quality")` on 2026-08-27 returned **1,113** and **3,759** stations, against roughly 4,400 when every request succeeds. Nothing in the return value says which is which.

That is a problem specifically because of what consumes it. `registry.harvest_stations` gives every source a `StationCatalog` with an `error` field (`registry.py:522-529`) so a dead source is visible to the weekly Archive harvest:

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad source must not sink the others
    logger.warning("[%s] station lookup failed: %s", key, exc)
    return StationCatalog(source=key, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", ...)
```

BOM never raises, so `error` stays empty and the harvest records a truncated Australian catalog as a clean success. BOM is currently the only source that can do this, because it is the only one making N requests per call.

## What to build

Track the parameter types that failed and let the caller see them. Roughly:

- Collect failed types in a list instead of only logging each one.
- If **every** request failed, raise rather than return `[]`, so `StationCatalog.error` fires and the harvest reports the source as down.
- If **some** failed, surface it: either a summary warning naming the types (cheapest) or a structured field the harvest can record, so a partial catalog is distinguishable from a complete one.

The existing per-request `try/except` should stay. A partial Australian catalog is better than none; it just should not be silently indistinguishable from a full one.

- [ ] A run where every parameter-type request fails raises instead of returning an empty list
- [ ] A run where some requests fail reports which types were lost, not just a count of dropped rows
- [ ] A fully successful run behaves exactly as it does today

ISSUE TITLE: BOM stations() returns a silently partial catalog when KiWIS 500s
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters

`BOMCollector.stations()` (added in #276) issues one `getStationList` request per BOM parameter type, because an unfiltered response leaves `parametertype_name` blank on ~76% of rows. Each request is wrapped in its own `try/except` (`collectors/bom.py:186-193`): a failure is logged as a warning and the loop continues.

BOM's KiWIS gateway returns intermittent 500s. #208 noted this when the issue was written, and it is still true: two consecutive live runs of `stations(variable="water_quality")` on 2026-08-27 returned **1,113** and **3,759** stations, against roughly 4,400 when every request succeeds. Nothing in the return value says which is which.

That is a problem specifically because of what consumes it. `registry.harvest_stations` gives every source a `StationCatalog` with an `error` field (`registry.py:522-529`) so a dead source is visible to the weekly Archive harvest:

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad source must not sink the others
    logger.warning("[%s] station lookup failed: %s", key, exc)
    return StationCatalog(source=key, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", ...)
```

BOM never raises, so `error` stays empty and the harvest records a truncated Australian catalog as a clean success. BOM is currently the only source that can do this, because it is the only one making N requests per call.

## What to build

Track the parameter types that failed and let the caller see them. Roughly:

- Collect failed types in a list instead of only logging each one.
- If **every** request failed, raise rather than return `[]`, so `StationCatalog.error` fires and the harvest reports the source as down.
- If **some** failed, surface it: either a summary warning naming the types (cheapest) or a structured field the harvest can record, so a partial catalog is distinguishable from a complete one.

The existing per-request `try/except` should stay. A partial Australian catalog is better than none; it just should not be silently indistinguishable from a full one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run where every parameter-type request fails raises instead of returning an empty list
- [ ] A run where some requests fail reports which types were lost, not just a count of dropped rows
- [ ] A fully successful run behaves exactly as it does today
- [ ] Tests cover all three cases with a mocked client (see `tests/test_collectors/test_stations.py`, which already mocks per-parameter-type payloads)

ISSUE TITLE: BOM stations() returns a silently partial catalog when KiWIS 500s
ISSUE DESCRIPTION:
## Why this matters

`BOMCollector.stations()` (added in #276) issues one `getStationList` request per BOM parameter type, because an unfiltered response leaves `parametertype_name` blank on ~76% of rows. Each request is wrapped in its own `try/except` (`collectors/bom.py:186-193`): a failure is logged as a warning and the loop continues.

BOM's KiWIS gateway returns intermittent 500s. #208 noted this when the issue was written, and it is still true: two consecutive live runs of `stations(variable="water_quality")` on 2026-08-27 returned **1,113** and **3,759** stations, against roughly 4,400 when every request succeeds. Nothing in the return value says which is which.

That is a problem specifically because of what consumes it. `registry.harvest_stations` gives every source a `StationCatalog` with an `error` field (`registry.py:522-529`) so a dead source is visible to the weekly Archive harvest:

```python
except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad source must not sink the others
    logger.warning("[%s] station lookup failed: %s", key, exc)
    return StationCatalog(source=key, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", ...)
```

BOM never raises, so `error` stays empty and the harvest records a truncated Australian catalog as a clean success. BOM is currently the only source that can do this, because it is the only one making N requests per call.

## What to build

Track the parameter types that failed and let the caller see them. Roughly:

- Collect failed types in a list instead of only logging each one.
- If **every** request failed, raise rather than return `[]`, so `StationCatalog.error` fires and the harvest reports the source as down.
- If **some** failed, surface it: either a summary warning naming the types (cheapest) or a structured field the harvest can record, so a partial catalog is distinguishable from a complete one.

The existing per-request `try/except` should stay. A partial Australian catalog is better than none; it just should not be silently indistinguishable from a full one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run where every parameter-type request fails raises instead of returning an empty list
- [ ] A run where some requests fail reports which types were lost, not just a count of dropped rows
- [ ] A fully successful run behaves exactly as it does today
- [ ] Tests cover all three cases with a mocked client (see `tests/test_collectors/test_stations.py`, which already mocks per-parameter-type payloads)
